name: graph-first-test-pending
body:
AC5 SPINE TARGET — resolved (spec-review feedback-1 on this note) [with coordinator]. The requirement's coherence-test acceptance criterion (AC5) is ALREADY met by a real test in the branch graph: `rust.apg.tests.e2e.graph_first_rule_stated_in_navigator_prompt_and_guide` (`src/main.rs:5053-5116`). It asserts the navigator prompt states the graph-first ordering (`Graph first, then file read`), that the rule names both artifact classes (`In the graph:` / `Not in the graph:`), that `AGENTS.md` carries the qualifier (`confirm and anchor` / `do not discover graph facts`), and that `agent-builder.md` rule 5 propagates the ordering to generated agents — exactly AC1–AC5. The component carries an `implemented-by` edge to it; no planned test node is needed and the plan-writer must not declare one.

The earlier body of this note was wrong: it claimed the test did not exist in the scanned branch graph and deferred it to a future planned Implementation node. In fact it has existed since the graph-first-prompt change-set; the FQN renders language-rooted as `rust.apg...` in this branch's graph, so it resolves.

The read-guard test it sits beside is `rust.apg.tests.e2e.installed_agent_prompts_state_file_access_read_guard` (its `fn` at `src/main.rs:4996`; the graph reports the enclosing unit as `src/main.rs:4988-5051`). The earlier citation of `src/main.rs:4877-4940` was incorrect.

0.17.0 boundary-list shrink: the existing AC5 test asserts only the presence of the two class labels, not their contents, so it continues to pass after the not-in-graph list shrinks (both labels remain). If the shrink must be pinned by assertion, the new assertions belong in the SAME existing test (`rust.apg.tests.e2e.graph_first_rule_stated_in_navigator_prompt_and_guide`) — never a new test and never a planned code node. See `requirements.requirement.graph-first-navigation` and `requirements.note.graph-first-baseline-correction`.
